newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl's office denies he threatened to resign.
newsitem.headline: Kohl's office denies he threatened to resign.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl did not threaten to resign last week during budget talks between his Christian Democrats and their junior coalition partners the Free Democrats, a chancellery spokesman said on Monday.
The spokesman was denying a report in the Hamburger Morgenpost saying that Kohl made such threats several times during talks on how best to plug growing gaps in the 1997 budget.
The newspaper said Kohl made the threat twice during talks last Sunday, and twice more in a similar session on Tuesday. "That is not true," the spokesman said.
Kohl, who has been chancellor since 1982 and has already announced he will be his party's candidate in the 1998 elections, has threatened to resign on several occasions in the past.

Last week's budget wrangle came as Finance Minister Theo Waigel rowed back from a plan to revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves to generate windfall profits that could be used to offset some of Germany's outstanding debt, in a bid to qualify for European monetary union at the start in 1999.
Frustrated in that effort, Waigel is now focusing on spending cuts.
